Build a NestedScale from a flat table of leaves

Source: R/scale-construct.R
scale_from_leaftable.Rd

The general constructor. Takes a wide data.frame with one row per leaf (the finest member) and one column per frame, and returns a NestedScale.

Usage

scale_from_leaftable(
  leaftable,
  frames,
  leaf = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  default_weight = NULL,
  members = NULL,
  name = "",
  desc = "",
  attributes = NULL,
  aliases = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

leaftable

data.frame with one row per leaf, one column per name in frames, and optionally numeric weight columns.

frames

Ordered character vector of frame names, coarsest first. Each must be a column of leaftable.

leaf

Name of the leaf column: the column that identifies the leaves, one unique code per row. Defaults to a column called "leaf" if present, otherwise to the finest frame (the last entry of frames).

weights

Character vector naming the weight columns. Defaults to all numeric columns that are neither frames nor reserved names.

default_weight

The weight used when a caller does not name one. Defaults to the first entry of weights.

members

Optional named list giving the ordered code vocabulary per frame. Derived from leaftable when NULL (first-appearance order).

name, desc

Short name and description.

attributes

Optional table of per-member physical attributes keyed by (frame, member); see attach_attributes_scale() for the columns.

aliases

Optional table of alternative labels keyed by (frame, member); see attach_aliases_scale() for the columns.

labels

Optional table of display names keyed by (frame, member, variant); see attach_labels_scale() for the columns.

...

Further named entries merged into meta (e.g. source).

Value

A NestedScale.

Details

Blank strings ("") in frame columns are normalised to NA, meaning "this leaf has no code at this frame" – partial coverage is normal in real classification tables.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  section = c("A", "A", "A", "B"),
  group   = c("A1", "A1", "A2", "B1"),
  item    = c("A11", "A12", "A21", "B11"),
  gva     = c(100, 200, 300, 400)
)
scale_from_leaftable(df, frames = c("section", "group", "item"))
#> NestedScale: <unnamed>
#> Frames (3, coarsest first):
#>   - section (2)
#>     - group (3)
#>       - item (4)
#> Leaves: 4
#> Weights: gva (default: gva)
